default.notes: Apply for a visa in advance at an Iraqi embassy or consulate — requirements vary by mission and approval from Baghdad can take several weeks. The Kurdistan Region operates a separate, broader entry regime whose stamps are not valid for federal Iraq.

groups.notes: Eligible for a 60-day visa on arrival (about USD 77, payable in cash) at Iraq's international airports and main border crossings under the March 2021 reform.
Citizens of Gulf Cooperation Council states can generally obtain a visa on arrival — conditions and permitted stays are set bilaterally; confirm with an Iraqi mission before travel.

IQ.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Iraqi citizens.

IL.notes: Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Iraq, and evidence of travel to Israel in another passport can also lead to refusal of entry.

IR.notes: Under the bilateral agreement Iranian citizens travelling by air can enter Iraq without a visa — an arrangement aimed mainly at pilgrimage traffic; land-border arrivals may still need a visa, so confirm before travel.

TR.notes: Turkish citizens are generally issued visas on arrival, and the Kurdistan Region admits them freely — terms have changed several times, so confirm with an Iraqi mission before travel.
